title: Residential fires safety
titleCn: 住宅火灾安全讲座（奥克兰消防官）

paragraphs.text: Section two.
You will hear a talk by a fire safety officer at a local community center in Auckland, New Zealand.
First, you have some time to look at questions eleven to sixteen on page three.
Now listen carefully and answer questions eleven to sixteen.
Well, to start with, thank you all for coming. For the purposes of today's talk, I'll just be focusing on residential fires. In other words, fires that occur at home.
Now, as you know, we've got a lot of old houses made out of wood in Auckland, but, um, these don't actually rate as particularly high on our statistics for serious fires.
In fact, serious fires mainly occur in residential housing in areas with families on low incomes.
This may be the case for a number of reasons, but a factor that stands out is that many of these houses have no smoke alarms.

We also see a good number of serious fires in property which is rented out, and again, there's, uh, there's an absence of smoke alarms here too. The stories you read in the paper about empty houses being set alight by vandals,
actually it's very rare. So whatever materials your house is made of, it's the furnishings inside that are flammable, and that's why a smoke alarm is invaluable.
Something else is that many serious house fires in Auckland are not reported until it's too late. Probably because
for the reason that the majority often break out between two and four AM and, um, residents don't tend to be awake, and you won't get many witnesses at that time to report it either.
So don't hesitate to call the fire service, even if it's a small fire.
Too many people assume that they can extinguish the flames by themselves and have no idea how swiftly they can spread.
Even if they've got a domestic fire extinguisher, by the time they've worked out how to use it, it's too late.
What you need to do is remain calm so you'll stand a better chance of taking the appropriate action to save your property. I'll come back to this later.
Now, most people have matches in their homes, and it goes without saying that care should be taken. But, uh,
they are one of the most common causes behind house fires, even though we're aware of the danger.
What we've been seeing recently is, uh,
actually fires that are started by candles.

I know they can look nice, but they're also dangerous when you put them near flammable material. After a call-out, people are usually in a state of disbelief. How can such a small flame be responsible for all that damage?
Just never leave them unattended.
We all know that burning cooking oil is a major cause of household fire, far more so than fires resulting from equipment such as portable heaters and electric blankets.
Having said that, the danger of plugging too many electrical devices into a wall socket is frequently underestimated. So it's, uh, vital that electrical circuits are never overloaded.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions seventeen to twenty on page four.
Now listen and answer questions seventeen to twenty.

Anyway, you'll do yourself a big favor if you get a smoke alarm installed in your property, whether you've got a big house or a small one. The best place is in the hallway near the bedrooms, in the bedrooms themselves, plus the lounge. Fitting a smoke alarm to the ceiling or wall is, to be honest, a very simple procedure, simpler than most people imagine.

Once this is done, you can also get your family together for a chat about how you're going to get out of the house if a fire occurs. It's the kind of thing people put off talking about. It's not that they've forgotten. It's just that they think it'll never happen to them. But you need to talk about it sooner rather than later.
Um, I should have mentioned before about maintaining your smoke alarm. So, uh, dust does affect smoke alarms and you want them to work properly. So clean them once a month to be on the safe side.

And if you're still in doubt about where to put them or what kind to buy, contact your local fire service. They'll come to your house and discuss it with you. And there's no charge for this service, so it's well worth organizing. Well, the next thing I'd like to talk about...
That is the end of section two.
You now have half a minute to check your answers.
